Missing from the old documentation#

  • Bug-report flow (Report a problem → admin bell + opt-in email → resolve → reporter notified) is not described in docs/user-guide.md; code: app/views/reports.py:20-125, app/templates/base.html:1555-1606.
  • Directory sign-in details: a successful bind for a new user creates the account with the global default profile (readonly unless changed) and, when approval is required, disabled with the "awaiting administrator approval" message — app/services/auth_store.py:84,201-212,558-597, app/auth/routes.py:63-67,120-131. User guide §1 only covers the import/sync path.
  • Password-reset specifics (1-hour link, local accounts only, the non-revealing message, "Email is not configured…" banner) — app/auth/routes.py:223-282, app/templates/auth/forgot.html.
  • Per-route rate limits beyond sign-in: 2FA 10/min, forgot 5/15 min, reset 10/15 min — app/auth/routes.py:171,224,259.
  • Profile page preferences: bookmark grouping order, language picker semantics (withdrawn language kept and flagged), per-user Calendar switch (admins only), per-product banner — app/templates/auth/profile.html:35-194, app/auth/routes.py:346-434.
  • UI language resolution order (saved preference → browser Accept-Language → English, limited to languages the admin offers) — app/services/ui_locale.py.
  • Global home Infrastructure-health strip (HA nodes, Git repo, backup server; Global-only endpoint) — app/templates/_infra_health.html, app/views/monitoring.py:291-302.
  • Global home certificate card counts already-expired certificates in "expiring ≤30d" (not_after <= now+30d, no lower bound) — app/views/global_home.py:104-110.
  • Hardware-scan notifications are only raised when at least one device failed — app/views/monitoring.py:246-262.
  • Notification bell preview size (8) and page size (100), 30-second poll — app/__init__.py:794, app/views/notifications.py:26, app/templates/base.html:1570.

Stale or wrong in the old documentation#

  • docs/user-guide.md:68 "Change it on first login (Profile → password)": the Profile page has no password form; its About card links to Settings → Change Password (app/templates/auth/profile.html:229-231, form at app/templates/settings/index.html:4832-4866).
  • docs/user-guide.md:4867-4869 "Add a device from its own page or from Bookmarks → Devices; Adopt takes an existing team bookmark and files it on your own panel": no device page posts to the bookmarks endpoints (only base.html and partials/bookmarks_panel.html do); /bookmarks/devices only feeds the Add-bookmark dialog; adopt turns a device from the inventory lens into the user's own personal bookmark (app/views/bookmarks.py:483-499, app/services/bookmarks.py:628-651).
  • docs/user-guide.md:4864 lists a view bookmark kind: the model has it (app/models_bookmarks.py:51-53) but the Add-bookmark dialog offers only Device and Link (app/templates/base.html:1140-1143), so it cannot be created from the UI.
  • docs/user-guide.md:4896-4902 "groups by any of seven modes … folder, zone, line, department, segment, kind, tag": the panel now has fixed roots (Favourites, Folders, Shared) plus ONE inventory lens whose nesting order (six dimensions, default Line › Zone › Department) is set per user on the profile page (app/services/bookmarks.py:54-69,434-509, app/views/bookmarks.py:254-359).
  • docs/user-guide.md:4858 and :4909 — two sections both numbered "38.1".
  • docs/user-guide.md:4987 (and app/services/concept_map.py:27-28) "concept keys appear in the URL (/map/?c=waf)": nothing reads a c parameter — app/views/concept_map.py:18-27 ignores query args and app/static/js/concept_map.js has no URL handling. — Fixed (GS-16, commit 4e6b062: the docstring now cites the real deep link /map/#cm-c-<key>).
  • docs/management-overview.md:57 "Version 1.0" vs VERSION 2.10.1.
  • docs/management-overview.md:83 "The default administrator password is documented": there is no default; the installer asks for it (min 8, installers/install-satom.sh:808-813) or the guided setup/app generate one into a 0600 file (installers/satom-setup.sh:213, app/__init__.py:2424-2443).
  • docs/management-overview.md:84 "no high-availability pair of the manager itself yet": HA exists (app/views/ha.py, deploy/satom-reconciler.service, deploy/satom-ha-datasync.sh, top-bar PRIMARY/STANDBY badge app/templates/base.html:106-117).
  • docs/management-overview.md:12-15,92 describe only FortiWeb/FortiADC and "a Redis cache": four products are managed (app/branding.py:_FALLBACK); Redis is optional, default memory:// (app/config.py:64), and the installer does not install it (installers/install-satom.sh:259-262).
  • README.md:5 "FortiAuthenticator planned": it is a live ADOM with its own blueprint (app/views/fac.py:39, app/branding.py comment "Promoted … 2026-08-05").
  • README.md:43,67 "Three workspaces — Global, FortiWeb, FortiADC": five ADOMs (app/branding.py, sidebar branches app/templates/base.html:308-1025).
  • README.md:79 "Git source of truth … auto-published to git": replaced by the content-addressed local SoT store (app/services/sot_store.py docstring "Replaces the git-backed reports/ history (retired 2026-08-05)", app/models_sot.py).
  • docs/engineering.md:161-162 "Three products share one app" and :176-178 "fortiweb sees everything except fortiadc": scoping is now an inclusion rule — FortiWeb sees its own rows plus unscoped rows, every other product only its own (app/services/product_scope.py:1-30).
  • docs/engineering.md:81 "Redis (local) backs Flask-Limiter": optional; default memory:// (app/config.py:60-64).
  • docs/engineering.md:75 "the main unit runs as the unprivileged satom user": the shipped unit says User=root (deploy/satom.service:7); the de-privilege is a drop-in written by the installer / deploy/migrate-deprivilege.sh:115-135 (installers/install-satom.sh:1650-1690). Correct in effect only after the installer/migration.
  • docs/overview.md:12 "administers a fleet of FortiWeb appliances" (four products now); docs/overview.md:34-37,54-55 contain internal host/container identifiers and describe Redis as part of the stack — must not be republished.
  • docs/overview.md:59-60 hardening claims (ProtectSystem=strict etc.) are not in deploy/satom.service, nor in the drop-ins written by installers/install-satom.sh / deploy/migrate-deprivilege.sh; in the snapshot only deploy/satom-metrics.service and deploy/satom-integrations.service carry them.

Inconsistencies between code, UI and configuration#

  • Session Lock is not enforced. Settings → General → "Session Lock (minutes)" ("Inactivity before the session expires and re-asks for the password", app/templates/settings/index.html:80-85) is saved (app/services/settings_store.py:21,54,176,299) but no code reads session_timeout; no PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME is set while sessions are made permanent (app/__init__.py:139,151,241, app/views/product.py:43,58), so Flask's default lifetime applies. Documented as such in first-login → Advanced. — Fixed (GS-01, decision: Session Lock enforced as an idle timeout; background polls do not extend it, idle sign-out is audited, Bearer tokens unaffected, commit b38f3da).
  • Password minimum differs by path. Reset link and the (unused) profile POST require ≥ 8 characters (app/auth/routes.py:270,298); Settings → Change Password only rejects an empty password (app/views/settings.py:1238-1240) although its placeholder says "At least 8 characters" (app/templates/settings/index.html:~4850). Installer enforces 8; INSTALL.md says the guided setup requires ≥10 and three classes. — Partly fixed (GS-02, AD-03, AD-04, AD-05: one 8-character minimum on every web password path incl. Settings → Change Password; the INSTALL.md guided-setup wording is not addressed, commit 4053cb7). — Fixed (GS-03, decision: one policy of 12–1024 characters, length only, in every web path, the CLI and both installers incl. the guided setup; 3-class rule dropped, commit 1813453).
  • Dead profile password handler. /auth/profile POST still implements a password change (app/auth/routes.py:291-307) but auth/profile.html contains no form posting to it. — Fixed (GS-04, commit 4e6b062).
  • Directory JIT profile: app/auth/routes.py:9-10 docstring says new directory users are provisioned with the operator profile; app/services/auth_store.py:561,581 actually assigns the global default profile (fallback readonly, :84). — Fixed (GS-05, commit 4e6b062).
  • Notifications "Clear all" has no UI. POST /notifications/clear deletes rows (app/views/notifications.py:45-50; service docstring "the page's 'Clear all'", app/services/notifications.py:133) but neither notifications/index.html nor base.html posts to it. — Fixed (GS-06, decision: Clear all button with confirm + CSRF on the Notifications page, commit e5ed5fe).
  • Search shortcut: the top-bar button title is "Search (/)" (app/templates/base.html:205) but the / key handler exists only on the Search page (app/templates/search/index.html:212-214). — Fixed (GS-07, commit e5ed5fe).
  • Infra card points to a renamed settings entry: "Settings → SoT & Backup" (app/templates/_infra_health.html:110) vs the current group "Source of Truth & Backup" → Configuration SoT / Backup Server (app/templates/settings/_nav.html:87-89). The same card hard-codes an internal backup-host name in UI strings (_infra_health.html:41,115). — Fixed (GS-08, GS-09, commit 4e6b062).
  • Appliances page reachability: the sidebar entry sits in the Administrator group gated on user_manage (app/templates/base.html:369,444,550,628,989) while appliances.index is login_required only and appliances.create needs only config_write (app/views/appliances.py:171-172,247-249) — operators can register appliances only by typing the URL. — Partly fixed (DV-06: the Appliances list/detail now require appliances.view instead of sign-in only; sidebar placement and the config_write create gate unchanged, commit a66b23f). — Fixed (GS-10, decision: Appliances entry moved to the Global / Fleet groups for appliances.view holders; create stays config_write, commit e5ed5fe).
  • Backups vault vs backups.view: every backups route requires coarse backup (app/views/backups.py:30-48,103-106), which derives only from backups.create/backups.restore (app/permissions.py:140); a profile with only backups.view cannot open the vault list. — Fixed (GS-11, decision: index/list gated on backups.view; create/upload/delete stay backup, download backups.create, commit 7b2cf01).
  • Concept Map filtering relies only on the __required_permission__ stamp of app/auth/decorators.require_permission (app/services/concept_map.py:713-732, app/auth/decorators.py:22). Pages gated any other way are listed regardless — e.g. monitoring.satom (on the map, concept_map.py:264) is restricted in-body to the Global ADOM (app/views/monitoring.py:171-181), and rbac.require_permission (app/rbac.py:32-44) does not stamp the attribute. The map's per-user filter is therefore best-effort. — Fixed (GS-12, commit ae2a8c2: __global_only__ stamp, such pages are linked with the Global ADOM pinned; GS-13: the rbac.require_permission part is moot, app/rbac.py is used by no view).
  • Templates module docstring stale: app/views/templates.py:1-6 says "Admin-only … applying a template … is intentionally not wired here yet", but the module has granular-permission routes for save/apply/approve (app/views/templates.py:77-359). — Fixed (GS-14, commit 4e6b062).
  • Placeholder wording: app/views/product.py:22-24 and app/branding.py:9-10 still call FortiAuthenticator/FortiAnalyzer "placeholder ADOMs", while both are seeded placeholder: False with real homes (app/branding.py:_FALLBACK, app/views/product.py:13-21). — Fixed (GS-15, commit 4e6b062).

Not documented (and why)#

  • Two-factor enrolment screen details beyond the button labels (QR flow JS) and the admin-side "clear 2FA" procedure — owned by settings / users-and-profiles.
  • Settings → Authentication (LDAP/AD/RADIUS configuration, group sync, approval gate) and Access Control — owned by the administration agent (settings, users-and-profiles); first-login only states the user-visible effects.
  • Turbo/per-tab internals (X-ADOM, _adom) are mentioned only in an :::advanced block of adoms-and-products.
  • The concept-map page counts quoted in the old guide (109 mapped / 141 excluded) — not verifiable without running the app; omitted.
  • Infrastructure-health internals (peer /healthz, SFTP statvfs) and the hard-coded backup-host name — omitted to avoid internal identifiers.

Classification /classification/, POST /save Zones/Lines/Departments with cascading rename and guarded delete (classification.py:55-134) users.manage classification
Line Profiles /line-profiles/, /save, /delete Declare segments, cert class, WPP template per line (line_profiles.py:63-150) users.manage line-profiles
Structure /structure/, POST /structure/save Dependency tree, registry/CLI/build coverage, admin overlay (structure.py:43-209) view: login; overlay: users.manage structure

Missing from the old documentation#

  • The fleet-wide WAF pages (Overview, Inventory, Profiles, Coverage, Artifacts, Exceptions) and their ZIP export are absent from docs/user-guide.md (waf.py:1-31; waf_export.py:713-743).
  • The WAF Artifacts section (Object types, Inventory, Device audit; upload/author/capture, verdicts ok/borrowed/at-risk/blocked, fork-on-save, refresh of the policy→artifact index) has no user-guide section. Only two rows in the 2.0 upgrade table mention it (user-guide.md:5874-5876; artifacts.py:1-49, 390-1176; artifact_refs.py:343-365).
  • The /signatures catalog sync page is undocumented. The guide only describes the FortiADC signatures page (user-guide.md:1591; signatures.py:139-181).
  • Exception versioning, rollback, restore, deploy to other FortiWebs, the impact report, guarded delete, split and "Analyse before implementing" are not in §9 (exceptions.py:261-345, 399-438, 559-645).
  • WPP deep clone, Save as template and "Hide default (predefined) profiles" are not in §8 (web_protection.py:415-576).
  • Server Objects certificate Import (SSH-only stores) and Generate, including the key-match and read-back checks (server_objects.py:172-247; overview.html:65-102).
  • The Configuration sections / seven WAF protection-area browser, "Other Objects", singleton detection, inline editor and per-type template library (section_config.py; config_sections.py:445-453, 641-669).
  • Template Library approval history, the WPP auto-deploy on approve, and job end states (templates.py:98-134, 313-335).
  • Fleet Objects modes, columns, the 1000-row search cap and the CSV name. The guide has one line (user-guide.md:1043-1045; fleet_objects.py:136).
  • Policy list: clone-history badge, Clone report page and its access rule, interface-binding table, file-backed objects gate ("Clone anyway — SKIP…"), additive mode (on by default), same-chassis warning, regex filters with a ReDoS watchdog, Check live health, the New Server Policy create form (policies.html:21-604; workspace.py:444-462, 594-618, 819-875; policy_ops.py:638-669, 1146-1343, 1556-1564).
  • Wizard: multi-domain batches with a shared pool, department filter, bind an existing pool or copy members, all-or-nothing batch refusal (spo_wizard.html:45-121; services/spo_wizard.py:718-856).
  • Naming page: which consumers honour the patterns (Exceptions WPP clone name, Certificate Manager name) and that the FortiADC catalog has no consumer (wpp_clone_flow.py:36-51; cert_manager.py:476-483; grep render_names).
  • Classification: the per-row editor with cascading rename, guarded delete, adopt "In use but not in this catalog", and baseline-combo absorption (classification_ops.py; classification/index.html). The guide only mentions the page in §26.14 (user-guide.md:3201-3202).
  • Line Profiles has no user-guide section, only a passing link (user-guide.md:263; line_profiles.py; services/line_profiles.py).
  • Structure page (tree, registry cross-reference, per-build "Serves it?", CLI-only elements, clone gap, admin overlay) is undocumented (structure.py:43-209).

Stale or wrong in the old documentation#

  • user-guide.md:244-245 lists the columns Deployment Mode and Monitor Mode. The actual columns are Policy Name, Virtual Server, Server Pool, Protection Profile, HTTP Service, HTTPS Service, Status (policies.html:190-197).
  • user-guide.md:258-259 describes a "⏰ Schedule" control. No workspace template contains one.
  • user-guide.md:249 says "Edit opens the FortiWeb-style form". The form is inline on the detail page and there is no Edit button (policy_detail.html:158-175).
  • user-guide.md:372 describes a "Clone / Migrate" button. The real entries are the row menu and the bulk bar (policies.html:175-180, 260-262).
  • user-guide.md:399-464: "only if missing", "reuse a destination profile" and the whole "new, compare and decide" flow are not reachable from the UI. wpp_only_if_missing, dst_wpp and wpp_decisions are JSON-only, and wpp-compare has no UI caller (workspace.py:343-366, 388).
  • user-guide.md:471-486, 506-508, 519-522 describe certificate-material copy, backend probes, a reconciliation switch and a worker count as user choices. None has a UI control (workspace.py:333-357).
  • user-guide.md:276-277: the wizard Preview is said to be safe "at any permission level", but it posts to /apply, which requires config_write (spo_wizard.html:677-681; spo_wizard.py:154-155).
  • user-guide.md:5899-5980 (§41.8/41.9, clone dialog) sit under "## 43" and say "Workspace → Policies". The UI calls it Server Policy.
  • server_policy.md:210 says shared objects are deleted "only on explicit opt-in". No opt-in exists; those objects are always kept (policy_graph.py:36-51, 163-166).
  • user-guide.md:527 lists the Server Objects menu as "Server, Service, SSL, Protected Hostnames, Lists, Global, Certificates". The code has Server, Protected Hostnames, Service, Traffic Mirror, Certificates, SSL Ciphers, Global, X-Forwarded-For, IP Group, and Virtual IP is under Network (server_objects.py:124-243).
  • user-guide.md:532-533 says uncurated fields get a raw-JSON escape hatch. The FortiWeb editor falls back to a text input; raw JSON exists only in the ADC editor (workspace/_fields.html:62-106).
  • user-guide.md:3455 places the Section Catalog in the FortiWeb ADOM sidebar. There is no sidebar entry. It is reached via the FortiWeb Sections button on the Template Library (templates/index.html:20-29).
  • user-guide.md:1044-1045 says the Fleet Objects any-field search runs "over the entire cache". It scans only server policies, WPPs and server pools (fleet_objects.py:136).
  • docs/wpp_exceptions.md:227-243 describes "Git-share" and "⤓ Sync from git". exception_sync.py does not exist and there is no such button.
  • docs/wpp_exceptions.md:198 describes an "Auto-bind to WPP sub-policy" checkbox. It is not in list.html, and the inject view never passes auto_bind (exceptions.py:548-551).
  • docs/wpp_exceptions.md:23-25 gives the location as "Operations → Clone → WPP" / "under Web Protection". The entry is WAF → "Exceptions & Signature" (base.html:791-794).
  • docs/wpp_exceptions.md:195, 285 and docs/web_protection_profile.md:175, 194 require "CONFIG_WRITE + unlock". There is no unlock step in these views.
  • docs/wpp_exceptions.md:283 and user-guide.md:642-643 say Purge / policy deletion removes every carve-out. Purge is previewed and only unbinds carve-outs no other policy uses (exceptions.py:221-244).
  • user-guide.md:654-655 calls the alignment report "exportable". There is no export route.
  • user-guide.md:662 says "pick the appliance, paste the ID". The appliance is resolved from the reference by default (attack_search.py:85-104).
  • user-guide.md:686 says "around twenty-two fields". PRIMARY_FIELDS has 26 (attack_log.py:271-283).
  • user-guide.md:816 says saving a draft on a shared profile "warns". The save route does no shared-profile check, and template-managed profiles are refused with 403 (exceptions.py:179-185).
  • user-guide.md:5593 (§41 "Folding") says "A closed Filter card still shows what is being filtered". The filter card no longer folds, as §41.7 (user-guide.md:5649) and the template say (adom_assets/index.html:255-262, 788-791). The two §41 sections contradict each other, and §41 contains two "Folding" sections.
  • user-guide.md:5453 says an unreachable backup server "reads as unknown, never as no backups". In code every device is then graded never pushed, because no folder is listed (adom_assets.py:528-541 with backup_server.py:81-104; grade(None, False) → "never"). — Fixed (FW-03, commit 62b395e).
  • user-guide.md:2257 (AppIDs): column references "are header names, or index numbers if you say the file has no header row". Unticking First row is a header has no server-side effect (see Inconsistencies). — Fixed (FW-33, commit f81eb6c).

Inconsistencies between code, UI and configuration#

  • Line Profiles are written under the wrong ADOM from their only menu entry. The page scopes profiles by g.product (line_profiles.py:27-29), and its only sidebar link is in the Global ADOM (base.html:464), where g.product is global (line_profiles is not in fortiweb_scoped, init.py:241-261). The wizard looks profiles up by appl.kind = fortiweb (spo_wizard.py:128). Profiles saved from the menu are therefore never read by the wizard, and the WPP-template dropdown is empty there, because templates are stamped with a concrete product (services/templates.py:188). Documented workaround: /line-profiles/?_adom=fortiweb. — Fixed (FW-01, commit 62b395e).
  • The line wizard ignores the Naming page. naming.render_names(web_address, None, product) passes no overrides (services/spo_wizard.py:187), while its own refusal text says "fix it in Settings -> Naming" (spo_wizard.py:197-198). Only the WPP-exception clone name and the Certificate Manager name honour saved patterns. — Fixed (FW-02, commit 62b395e).
  • Stored Assets: an unreachable backup server makes every device "never pushed". The banner promises "Backup columns below read "unknown", not "none"" (adom_assets/index.html:214), and the test named test_an_unreachable_server_reads_as_unknown_not_as_no_backups asserts nothing about rows (tests/test_adom_assets_and_sot_payload.py:761-770). — Fixed (FW-03, commit 62b395e).
  • AI advisory without the AI permission: POST /exceptions/<id>/advice calls the AI provider with @login_required only (exceptions.py:399-431). Attack Search's analyze and ask-field require advisor.use. — Fixed (FW-04, decision: SATOM's own advice stays open to protection.view; the AI opinion requires advisor.use, commit a77a442).
  • Unguarded delete still exposed: POST /exceptions/<id>/delete deletes without the impact check that the UI's guarded-delete enforces (exceptions.py:210-218). The UI no longer calls it. — Partly fixed (FW-06: delete and save now refuse a carve-out that does not belong to the URL's device; the missing impact check is not fixed, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (FW-05, commit a77a442).
  • Write buttons are never hidden by permission on the workspace, web_protection, exceptions, attack_search, server_objects, section_config, templates and artifacts templates (no current_user.can). Viewers get "Forbidden", or a 403 HTML page that breaks fetch JSON parsing. — Partly fixed (FW-07: write controls hidden or disabled without config_write on Server Policy list and editor, Exceptions, Web Protection, Server Objects and WAF artifacts; Attack ID proposal actions, the object editor, the signature policy editor and template buttons unchanged, commit fc99311).
  • WAF protection-area menus are shown to everyone but require config_write. The sidebar has no check (base.html:872-898), while every /configuration/ route requires CONFIG_WRITE (section_config.py:70-72, 94-96, 200-202). The docstring says reads are open to any signed-in user (section_config.py:14-16). — Fixed (FW-08, decision: the sidebar WAF areas are hidden without config_write and the docstring corrected, commit 21dfa4a).
  • Bulk clone drops the WPP suffix: the dialog sends wpp_suffix in bulk mode (policies.html:962), _parse_action never reads it (workspace.py:289-366), and the engine supports it (policy_ops.py:818). — Fixed (FW-09, commit 438fd6a).
  • Delete dialog text vs behaviour: "Shared objects (WPP, pool, certificate, service) are kept" (policies.html:676), but an unshared pool or virtual server is deleted (policy_graph.py:154-173). The delete preview maps always_skip, which the planner never emits (policies.html:1147-1148 vs policy_graph.py:60-69). — Fixed (FW-10, FW-11, commit 438fd6a).
  • New Server Policy form: no WPP field is rendered (workspace.py:118, 798, 802). The AppID selector reads appid_catalog, which the view never passes, and its app_id_pk is ignored (policy_new.html:22, 118; workspace.py:795-875). — Fixed (FW-12, FW-13, commit 438fd6a).
  • /workspace/<id>/browse/<path> relays any GET path to the device for any signed-in user. There is no allow-list, unlike cmdb-options (workspace.py:758-771). — Fixed (FW-14, decision: unused route and template removed, commit fc99311).
  • "Change Appliance" links to /workspace/, which redirects back to the current device (policies.html:82-84; workspace.py:154-157). — Fixed (FW-15, commit fc99311).
  • Wizard issues a certificate but the policy payload does not reference it (services/spo_wizard.py:624-626, 707-711). It binds the line's WPP template name without checking that the profile exists on the device (:709-710). — Fixed (FW-16, FW-17, commit 62b395e).
  • Template apply: the canary is devs[:1] of an unordered query, not "the first selected device" as the UI says (bulk.py:134-137, 237-238 vs templates/index.html:303). device_ids are not checked against visible_appliances (templates.py:219-224). WPP auto-deploy on approve targets every visible appliance with no product filter (templates.py:313-317). — Partly fixed (FW-19: device_ids are now checked against the user's visible devices, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (FW-18, FW-20, commit faaf761).
  • Template Library is linked only from the Administrator group (user_manage, base.html:1003-1018), but the route needs only operations.view (templates.py:53). Errors refer to a non-existent "Administrator → WPP Templates" (objedit.py:436-439; web_protection/overview.html:251). — Fixed (FW-21, FW-22, commit faaf761).
  • Config Compare says "the export has all of them", but fields are cut to 40 before export (config_compare/index.html:246 vs config_compare.py:525-526, 734-736). — Fixed (FW-23, commit f81eb6c).
  • Fleet Objects header says "(cached ~60s)", but reads are DB-first from the local store (fleet_objects/index.html:22-24 vs services/fleet_objects.py:209-238). — Fixed (FW-24, commit 14be709).
  • Server Objects refresh is login-only (server_objects.py:250-252), while the section refresh needs config_write (section_config.py:200-202). Both run the same full device sync. — Fixed (FW-25, decision: Server Objects and Server Policy refresh require config_write, buttons hidden without it, commit fc99311).
  • Section page ?device= is emitted by links (base.html:932) but ignored; the session device is used (section_config.py:108). — Fixed (FW-26, commit 21dfa4a).
  • Attack ID AI buttons are gated on advisor.enabled(), not on the user's advisor.use (attack_search.py:120; attack_drawer.js:303, 331). proposal/<pid>/dismiss has no appliance-visibility check, unlike apply (attack_search.py:1163-1177 vs 1117). — Partly fixed (FW-28: dismiss now requires the device to be visible, like apply, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (FW-27, commit f81eb6c).
  • The fleet Exceptions page posts back=exceptions, which _EXPORT_BACK omits (waf.py:520-521). — Fixed (FW-29, commit f81eb6c).
  • signature_policy.html:45 and web_protection.py:348-349 point to "Settings → Signatures". The menu is Administrator → Signatures (base.html:1014). — Fixed (FW-30, commit faaf761).
  • Structure firmware selector cannot work with JavaScript on: it submits through an inline onchange (structure/index.html:48), which the CSP blocks (script-src-attr 'none', init.py:1152). The Apply fallback is inside <noscript>. Only a hand-typed ?scope= works. — Fixed (FW-31, commit f81eb6c).
  • Structure view is login-only (structure.py:43-44), but its only entry point (sidebar API) is shown only with user_manage (base.html:1057-1059). — Fixed (FW-32, commit f81eb6c).
  • AppIDs "First row is a header" cannot be turned off: an unticked checkbox is not submitted, and _mapping_from_form defaults it to "1" (appids.py:245). A header-less file loses its first data row and the mapping is saved with has_header: true. — Fixed (FW-33, commit f81eb6c).
  • AppIDs device picker and assign use Appliance.query without visible_appliances (appids.py:46-48, 185-205). Maintenance devices are offered, and no check confirms that the policy exists. — Partly fixed (FW-34: picker and assign/unassign use visible devices only; the policy-existence check is not fixed, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (FW-35: FortiWeb policy names are checked against the local store, commit f81eb6c).
  • Classification refusal text counts appliances, baselines and segments but not line profiles, while the check uses the total including line profiles (classification_ops.py:268-270 vs 99). A line used only by a profile is refused with "used by 0 appliance(s), 0 baseline(s) and 0 segment(s)". The "In use by" badges also omit line profiles (classification/index.html:44-48). — Fixed (FW-36, FW-37, commit 14be709).
  • Stored Assets Files lists the 10 newest files per folder (backup_server.py:95), while the full-listing endpoint /adom-assets/files has no UI caller. delete-backup is not ADOM-scoped (adom_assets.py:140-158). — Partly fixed (FW-39: delete-backup is now limited to the active ADOM's device folders, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (FW-38: the table states when it shows only the newest files, commit 14be709).
  • The scheduled action artifact_refs describes itself as feeding "the migration coverage report on /artifacts/inventory" (scheduled_actions.py:315-321). That table was removed (user-guide.md:5876). — Fixed (FW-40, commit 14be709).
  • The waf_artifacts module docstring still says content is "pushed from the store to any destination", while artifacts.py:16-23 states there is no standalone push. — Fixed (FW-41, commit 14be709).
  • A legacy POST /settings/naming (USER_MANAGE) still writes both products' patterns into the FortiWeb key (settings.py:890-904). The Settings page has no Naming tab, though its preview JS remains (settings/index.html:5146-5160). — Fixed (FW-42, FW-43, commit 14be709).
  • line_profiles.save flashes with category 'error' (line_profiles.py:78-121), where the rest of the app uses 'danger'. — Fixed (FW-44, commit 62b395e).
  • Import form and Config Compare placeholders contain internal-looking host/device/policy names (server_objects/import.html:72; config_compare/index.html:52). They are not reproduced in the docs. — Fixed (FW-45, commit 14be709).

Not documented (and why)#

  • /workspace/<id>/browse/<path> (raw API browse): unlinked and internal. It is reported above as a security-relevant inconsistency. — Fixed (FW-14, decision: route removed, commit fc99311).
  • Field-by-field contents of the policy form, the WPP field reference (docs/web_protection_profile.md §2-4) and the per-type exception field reference (docs/wpp_exceptions.md §4): these are FortiWeb vendor data.
  • clone-exception and the unguarded /exceptions/<id>/delete: no UI uses them. They are mentioned only in Advanced or in this audit. — Fixed (FW-05: the unguarded delete route was removed, commit a77a442).
  • Unused templates web_protection/_menu.html, exceptions/index.html and workspace/index.html: dead code.
  • Artifact-upload modal on section pages: covered by a pointer to waf-artifacts.
  • /section-catalog/<id> and template-detail JSON shapes, the force delete flag, and NTP singleton internals: not exposed in the UI.
  • Stored Assets identity internals (chassis resolution order, §41.1): summarised in Advanced only.
  • Structure overlay node-path syntax beyond the documented example: it is derived from the built-in seed, and a guessed path would be invented.

Devices & Lifecycle#

Articles written (17): appliances, appliances-ha-clusters (child), rediscovery, device-health, backups, config-restore (child of backups), firmware, firmware-upgrade (child of firmware), upgrade-flow, upgrade-flow-change (child), upgrade-flow-execution (child), provisioning, system-provisioning-profiles, operator-console, container-ops, segments, capacity.

Extra slugs not in the master list: appliances-ha-clusters, config-restore, firmware-upgrade, upgrade-flow-change, upgrade-flow-execution.

Note on system-provisioning-profiles: app/views/profiles.py is permission profiles (RBAC, profiles.manage), not this topic. System provisioning profiles and baselines live in app/views/provisioning.py (+ services/baselines.py, services/bulk.py). The article documents those only.

  • user-guide.md:992 "a mandatory config backup": the pre-flight backup is best-effort and never blocks a flash (appliances.py:1392-1402); the synchronous (no-JS) path runs no pre-flight at all (appliances.py:1142-1172).
  • user-guide.md:997-999 "there is no way to schedule a flash without an approval": upgrade_schedule creates an enabled one-shot ScheduledAction with no CR (appliances.py:1180-1242), and the scheduled upgrade executor is a stub that never flashes (services/scheduled_actions.py:1450-1463). — Fixed (DV-11, decision: Schedule card and its route removed, the Upgrade page points to Upgrade Flow, existing rows untouched, commit 7b2cf01).
  • user-guide.md:1001-1002 "Boot partition management (view/boot the alternate partition) is a separate, gated page": the Boot Partition page flashes an older image to the alternate partition (appliances.py:1592-1704); it does not view/boot partitions and is not change-control gated (only config_write). — Partly fixed (DV-05: the gate is now appliances.apply instead of config_write; still no change-control gate, commit a66b23f). — Fixed (DV-09, decision: stays a CR-free emergency path; a live flash needs an explicit change-control-bypass acknowledgement and every attempt is audited, commit 7b2cf01).

The chunked endpoints exist (firmware.py:379-665) but no client calls them. — Fixed (DV-51: unused chunked upload endpoints removed, commit 82775c6).
  • user-guide.md:1719 (§20 "The operator console") documents the node-side satom CLI, not the web Device Console (views/console.py) — name collision with the operator-console article.
  • user-guide.md:5982 "System → Container operations": path is Global → Administrator → Container operations (base.html:472; same wrong string in runtime.py:109). — Fixed (DV-50: runtime string now reads Global → Administrator → Container operations, commit 82775c6).

Inconsistencies between code, UI and configuration#

  • Restore is gated users.manage, not backups.restore. Every restore route uses USER_MANAGE (appliances.py:1726-1825), while the catalog describes backups.restore as "Import/restore a configuration backup" (permissions.py:82). Import Backup is gated config_write (import_backup.py:41-53), not a backups key either. backups.restore therefore grants exactly what backups.create grants (both only derive coarse backup, permissions.py:140). — Fixed (DV-01, decision: every restore route requires users.manage and backups.restore; DV-02, decision: Import Backup gated on backups.restore; commit 7b2cf01).
  • appliances.* catalog vs gates. appliances.apply claims "Console, rediscovery, policy inspector, upgrade preparation & upgrade" (permissions.py:93-94), but the Inspector needs appliances.view (appliances.py:636), Upgrade Prep needs coarse backup (806, 819, 929) and Upgrade/Boot Partition/HA failover need config_write (1033-2103) — so any edit key (e.g. protection.edit) can flash firmware, and appliances.apply alone cannot run a pre-flight. appliances.view is not checked on the list or detail pages (171-173, 232-234), and backups.view is never checked anywhere. — Partly fixed (DV-05: Upgrade/Boot Partition/HA failover now require appliances.apply; DV-06: list, detail, test connection, datasheet, member roles and firmware reports now require appliances.view; both commit a66b23f. Inspector/Upgrade Prep catalog mismatch and backups.view unchanged). — Fixed (DV-03: appliances.apply description reworded, commit 82775c6; DV-04: Upgrade Prep gated on appliances.apply, commit 08bd8c2; DV-07, decision: backups.view gates the vault list, download needs backups.create, commit 7b2cf01).
  • The list's Edit dialog destroys data. It posts no HA or interface fields (appliances/index.html:430-521), and edit_save treats them as empty: _rebuild_interfaces deletes every documented interface (appliances.py:70-112, 399) and _parse_ha clears is_cluster/ha_mode/ha_vip on a non-member row (372-380). — Fixed (DV-08, commit 08bd8c2).
  • Boot Partition is not change-controlled while Upgrade and HA failover are (appliances.py:1642-1704 vs 1119-1136, 2063-2071). — Fixed (DV-09, decision: stays a CR-free emergency path with an explicit change-control-bypass acknowledgement and audited outcome, commit 7b2cf01).
  • Scheduled upgrade UI vs behaviour. The date field says "(UTC)" (upgrade.html, Schedule card) but is parsed in the configured time zone (appliances.py:1207-1214); the schedule needs no CR and the executor never flashes (scheduled_actions.py:1450-1463), while the page text says unattended flashing "is gated (an approved Change Request / explicit operator run)". — Fixed (DV-10: moot, the card is gone; DV-11, decision: Schedule card and route removed, scheduling goes through Upgrade Flow; commit 7b2cf01).
  • Install images offered for upgrade. compatible_images filters product and platform only (services/upgrade.py:377-388); Upgrade Flow filters image_kind == 'upgrade' (upgrade_flow.py:333). — Fixed (DV-12, commit 08bd8c2).
  • Pre-restore backup promise. restore.html says a pre-restore backup "is taken automatically"; it is REST-only (fetch_device_backup, no SSH fallback) and a failure does not stop the live restore (appliances.py:1892-1904). — Fixed (DV-13, decision: abort the live restore when the pre-restore backup fails unless "Restore without a pre-restore backup" is ticked, audited; page says REST-only; commit 7b2cf01).
  • Rediscovery start guard blocks only state == "running" (rediscovery.py:1367-1375): a second sweep can start while the first is in its deep or CLI pass, and start clears any pending stop flag (1390). — Fixed (DV-14, commit 08bd8c2).
  • Stop tooltip "No snapshot is written; the previous one is kept." (rediscover.html:57) is false once the sweep phase has finished (rediscovery.py:936-945, 1178-1186). — Fixed (DV-15, commit 82775c6).
  • 401 auth stop is FortiWeb-only: only _probe_fortiweb/status_check raise DeviceAuthError (rediscovery.py:707-712; clients/fortiweb.py:72-75); the FortiADC probe has no equivalent (rediscovery.py:814-817). — Fixed (DV-16, commit 08bd8c2).
  • Device health page vs alert engine. The page grades with the global capacity.warn_pct/crit_pct and the global stale budget (views/monitoring.py:36-45, 69, 93), while collect_for (alerts) resolves both per product (device_health.py:415-430) — the divergence the module says it exists to prevent (device_health.py:328-332). — Fixed (DV-17, commit 08bd8c2).
  • Hardware scan sends FortiWeb commands to every kind (services/hardware.py:17-23, 103-106; monitoring.py:274-275 scans all visible appliances incl. FortiAnalyzer/FortiAuthenticator). — Fixed (DV-18: FortiWeb rows only, button hidden elsewhere, commit 08bd8c2).
  • Firmware Reports visibility. Routes need only login (appliances.py:1269-1302); detail-page buttons are admin-only (detail.html:195-198) but the list page shows the button to everyone (index.html:21-23); flash_reports loads the focus appliance with Appliance.query.get (1300), bypassing the maintenance/ADOM visibility check. — Partly fixed (DV-06: routes now require appliances.view, commit a66b23f; DV-19: list/report and focus row limited to visible devices, commit fb6fc14. List-page button shown to everyone is unchanged). — Fixed (DV-20: Firmware Reports button shown to viewers on the detail page as on the list, commit 82775c6).
  • Firmware download/delete are not ADOM-scoped (FirmwareImage.query.get, firmware.py:668-696) while the list is (firmware.py:197-201). — Fixed (DV-21, commit fb6fc14).
  • "View Backups" from Global on a FortiADC device resolves in the FortiWeb ADOM (backups is in fortiweb_scoped, init.py:248-266), where a FortiADC row is not visible → 404 (models.py:605-622; product_scope.py:264-282). Derived from the code path; not run. — Fixed (DV-22, commit 08bd8c2).
  • Buttons shown to users who will get 403: Add/Edit/Delete on the list and Edit on the detail page (index.html:24-26, 160-174; detail.html:9), View Backups regardless of backup (detail.html:51, 55). — Fixed (DV-23, commit 82775c6).
  • List vs detail action sets: the list shows Inspector/Rediscovery icons for FortiWeb rows only (index.html:143-158); routes and the detail page support FortiADC too (appliances.py:624-630; detail.html:170-176). — Fixed (DV-24, commit 82775c6).
  • Field label "VDOM" (index.html:187, 332; detail.html:39) for what the code and the 401 hint call the ADOM (clients/fortiweb.py:9-13). — Fixed (DV-25: relabelled "ADOM (vdom)", commit 82775c6).
  • REST API /api/appliances create/update skip the ADOM kind check and delete skips identity retirement and datasheet removal (api/appliances.py:96-194 vs appliances.py:256-259, 471-491). — Partly fixed (DV-26: create/update now refuse a kind the active ADOM cannot assign, commit fb6fc14; delete still skips identity retirement and datasheet removal). — Fixed (DV-27: REST delete shares the UI delete's identity retirement and datasheet removal, commit 08bd8c2).
  • visible_appliances docstring says the FortiWeb ADOM sees "everything else"; code shows FortiWeb + empty kinds only (models.py:593-596 vs product_scope.py:278-282). — Fixed (DV-28, commit 82775c6).
  • app/templates/backups/index.html is not rendered by any view (dead template). — Fixed (DV-29: template deleted, commit 82775c6).
  • Helper findings (verified by the sub-writers, cited in their articles): Device Console menu entry hidden for operators who can use it (base.html:368 vs nav_console.html:20); read-only SSH Console Run needs appliances.apply (appliances.py:780); Device Console presets/TAC battery are FortiWeb-only for every kind (console.py:78; ssh_console.py:619); checkbox label mismatch (ssh_console.py:195 vs console/index.html:125); Capacity "Add model" always creates FortiWeb rows and validation messages disagree with checks (capacity.py:85, 108-132, 158; capacity/index.html:86 hard-coded 80 %); Segments label "Network Segment" vs "Network Segments" (base.html:566, 642, 1013); Device Provisioning page login-only, Preflight gated config_write but shows "Nothing blocks this run." to users without it (device_provision.py:66-111, 186-193; device_index.html:242-245); Approve/Reject drawn for everyone (provisioning/index.html:74-84); apply route ignores approval status (provisioning.py:200-212); "Entire fleet" counts visible appliances but the runner writes to all (provisioning.py:236-238 vs bulk.py:187-190); operations.view never checked (permissions.py:71); Upgrade Flow: only round 1 of a multi-round rollout executes (scheduled_actions.py:1914-1924; change_requests.py:553-586), FortiADC refused at stage 2 (scheduled_actions.py:94, 449-470), stage-3 Schedule drops rounds (change_requests.py:254-271), device-less change possible (upgrade_flow.py:1012-1040), Batched rollouts not ADOM-scoped (upgrade_flow.py:835-838), no chassis scoping in _eligible() (upgrade_flow.py:457-462). — Partly fixed (DV-38: Device Provisioning page/data/detail now require operations.view, commit a66b23f; DV-42: "Entire fleet" and baseline apply target only visible devices, commit fb6fc14; DV-48: Batched rollouts list only visible waves, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (DV-30, DV-33, DV-35, DV-36, DV-37, DV-40: commit 82775c6; DV-32, DV-34, DV-39, DV-44, DV-46, DV-47, DV-49: commit 08bd8c2; DV-31, decision: Run/presets hidden without appliances.apply, read-only notice; DV-41, decision: live apply refused unless the profile is approved; DV-45, decision: Upgrade Flow limited to FortiWeb, no ADC flash path; commit 7b2cf01. DV-43 "operations.view never checked" was rejected as false, no change).

Not documented (and why)#

  • Discovery-run plan / run / register routes (views/_discovery.py:16-24): unreachable from any page since they were removed from the UI; only the load card is documented (Advanced).
  • The exact CLI failover commands: the HA Failover page shows them from FAILOVER_TRANSPORT; the article points there instead of copying a table that can drift.
  • Internals of the API-library ingest, API matrix refresh, per-endpoint verdict ledger format, flash-report file layout and progress.json fields (implementation detail).
  • legacy Settings route that saves segments (settings.py:917, no form posts to it).
  • Hypervisor registration, IPAM/DNS backend setup (§21.1-21.5, §26.9): belong to Settings; linked only. Note: provisioning.md names Proxmox VE and VMware ESXi as supported hypervisor types (a product feature, settings/index.html:3154-3164), not internal infrastructure.
  • app/views/profiles.py (permission profiles): out of scope for this area (Administration → users-and-profiles).

Inconsistencies between code, UI and configuration#

  • FortiADC docstring vs behaviour: app/views/adc.py:15-19 says "Every write is … dry-run by default", but object_save and object_delete (adc.py:414-460, used by the list Delete button and Raw JSON save) write immediately. — Fixed (PR-01, commit e6a9a3e).
  • ADC/FAZ API consoles have no dry run, while the FAC console does (adc_api.py:170-180, faz_api.py:131-142 vs fac_api.py:153-157); section pages of ADC/FAZ are dry-run-first, so the most powerful write path is the least guarded. — Fixed (PR-02, decision: FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer console writes are dry-run unless Apply is ticked, as on FortiAuthenticator, commit 8098fd9).
  • API sidebar links vs page gates: ADC and FAZ show the API link only with user_manage (base.html:1060-1065), but /adc/api/ and /faz/api/ require only login (adc_api.py:62-64, faz_api.py:67-69); FAC shows its API entry to everyone (base.html:617-623). — Partly fixed (TR-06/PR-03: /adc/api/, /faz/api/ and /fac/api/ now require registry.view; sidebar link placement unchanged, commit a66b23f). — Fixed (PR-04: one API → Registry & console sidebar entry for all three ADOMs, gated on registry.view, commit 585d7c3).
  • ADC Signatures requires user_manage (adc.py:131-133) although it is read-only; the same data is visible without that permission at WAF Signature → Web Attack Signature (adc_menu.py:167-171). — Fixed (PR-05, decision: Signatures gated on protection.view and moved to the Web Application Firewall group, commit 585d7c3).
  • ADC first pool member cannot be added from the form: the child add-row form is built only from existing sibling rows (adc.py:205-219), never from CREATE_FIELDS (adc_objform.py:198-235, pool-member seed at :222); for an empty pool it offers only mkey, and form_save_row then rejects with "Missing required field(s): real_server_id" (adc.py:349-353). The message "No field template is known…" (adc/object.html:141) is unreachable because the blank sample always contains mkey (adc.py:211). — Fixed (PR-06, PR-07, commit 257a4de).
  • ADC object-editor allow-list cache not invalidated: adc_objform.known_logicals / _child_index are lru_cached (adc_objform.py:37-80) and adc_api.registry_toggle only clears the loader and adc_menu caches (adc_api.py:232-233); a disabled/re-enabled endpoint keeps its old editor allow-list until restart. adc_menu is also an lru_cache per process, so other workers keep a stale sidebar. — Fixed (PR-08, PR-09, commit 257a4de).
  • Unreachable FortiADC branch in the workspace: workspace.appliance lists virtual servers for kind == 'fortiadc' (app/views/workspace.py:174-177), but workspace is FortiWeb-scoped (app/__init__.py:246), not in adc_bps (:326-410), and visible_appliance_or_404 hides FortiADC devices from the FortiWeb ADOM (app/models.py:605-622). — Fixed (PR-10, commit e6a9a3e).
  • ADC ADOM has cap_firmware=True (branding.py:67) and firmware in adc_bps (__init__.py:376), but the FortiADC Administrator menu has no Firmware entry (base.html:369-397). — Fixed (PR-11, decision: firmware removed from the FortiADC ADOM allow-list, nothing flashes a FortiADC from the firmware library, commit 585d7c3).
  • FAZ device actions always target ADOM root: the view accepts adom (faz.py:278) but the toolbar never sends it (faz/section.html:524). — Fixed (PR-12, commit 257a4de).
  • Unreachable FAZ device buttons: dvmdb_device is in _READ_ONLY (faz_objform.py:36), so editable is false for the Devices tab and the Add Device (faz/section.html:99) and toolbar Edit buttons never render. — Fixed (PR-13, commit 257a4de).
  • registry_write comment is wrong: app/services/registry_write.py:40-43 says the FortiAnalyzer/FortiAuthenticator catalogs "have no editor", but faz_api.registry_save (faz_api.py:153-199) and fac_api.save_endpoint (fac_api.py:177-207) are editors that bypass registry_write validation; FAC's save has no duplicate check and silently re-enables a disabled row. — Fixed (PR-14, PR-16, commit 8098fd9; PR-15, decision: FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator catalog editors save through registry_write, commit 8098fd9).
  • FAC API page cannot disable an endpoint: the toggle route exists (fac_api.py:210-223) but the template only offers it for already-disabled rows (fac_api/index.html:80). — Fixed (PR-17, commit 8098fd9).
  • FAC API method selector does not disable write methods for users without registry.execute_write (fac_api/index.html:117-119), unlike ADC/FAZ; the server still refuses. — Fixed (PR-18, commit 8098fd9).
  • ADC console accepts PATCH server-side (adc_api.py:43) but the UI selector offers only GET/POST/PUT/DELETE (adc_api/index.html:270-275). — Fixed (PR-19, commit 8098fd9).
  • FAZ console always reports status=200 (faz_api.py:140) regardless of the JSON-RPC result code. — Fixed (PR-21, commit 8098fd9).
  • Audit asymmetry: ADC and FAZ consoles audit every executed call including reads (adc_api.py:172, faz_api.py:138); FAC audits writes only (fac_api.py:168-170). — Fixed (PR-22, decision: one policy, applied writes audited including failures, reads not audited, commit 8098fd9).
  • FAC gate allows pages its menu does not offer: backups and firmware are in fac_bps (__init__.py:464, :486) while the user guide says Device Backups are "Not offered in this workspace" (docs/user-guide.md:1632). — Fixed (PR-23, PR-24, decision: backups and firmware removed from the FortiAuthenticator ADOM allow-list, commit 585d7c3).
  • ADC naming patterns are not applied by the ADC object editor or the guided wizard (no use of services.naming in app/views/adc.py), although the Naming page lists FortiADC elements (app/services/naming.py:148-170). — Fixed (PR-25, decision: the Naming page marks FortiADC patterns as reference only, commit 585d7c3).
  • Orphan template: app/templates/product/fortiadc.html ("Basic structure ready") is never rendered (product.fortiadc_home redirects to adc.index, product.py:79-83). — Fixed (PR-26, commit e6a9a3e).

Not documented (and why)#

  • FortiADC/FortiAnalyzer CLI↔API coverage, Versions, Reconcile and Discovery details — shared machinery owned by the API registry article (api-registry); only pointed to from product-api-pages.
  • FortiAuthenticator metrics collectors (capacity, identity) from docs/fortiauthenticator.md §9 — belong to the monitoring/metrics area.
  • Appliance-detail device actions for FortiADC (test connection, VS inspector, SSH presets, upgrade prep, backups) listed in user guide §17.1 — belong to the devices area (appliances, backups, upgrade-flow).
  • FortiAuthenticator varchar(32) product-key migration (docs/fortiauthenticator.md §8) — developer history, not user documentation.
  • Shared Fleet/Automation/Administrator pages reachable from these ADOMs (monitoring, jobs, change requests, segments, firmware…) — owned by other areas; the product articles only list which entries each sidebar shows.

Inconsistencies between code, UI and configuration#

  • Search form submits appliance_id and obj_type (app/templates/search/index.html:40, 51) but the results view reads appliances and ignores the type (app/views/search.py:63-68) — both filters are no-ops. — Fixed (MO-01/MO-02, commit 8f8d97e).
  • Probe sweep cadence is stated three ways: action summary "Schedule EVERY 5 MINUTES" (app/services/scheduled_actions.py:310), service_monitor.py:36 "every five minutes", page note "every three minutes" (_probe_page.html:208); seed plan uses 3 min (deploy/satom_cli/cmd_fix.py:45-46) and DEFAULT_PROBE_INTERVAL_MIN=3 must be a multiple of the tick (deep_monitor.py:168-175). The add-probe form defaults Interval to 5 (_probe_page.html:408) — under the seeded 3-minute sweep that is effectively 6 minutes. — Fixed (MO-03/MO-04, commit 7d34b8c).
  • Scout resolves the typed "Published host" with net_guard MODE_FREE (app/services/scout_ladder.py:1211-1213) without checking monitoring.probe_free, which cert_inspect.py:40 and txn_trace.py:39 enforce for free targets. — Fixed (MO-05, decision: a typed host must be published by the appliance unless the user holds monitoring.probe_free or user_manage, commit 2705393).
  • Monitoring read views gate only on login_required (e.g. app/views/monitoring.py:153-154, metrics.py:126-127, monitor_probes.py:322-324, monitor_analytics.py:87-88, search.py:52-53, architecture.py:42-43), while their docstrings say "Reads need VIEW" (deep_monitor.py:17, monitor_analytics.py:12, monitor_reports.py:10); reach_batch.py:61-63 and scout.py:129-131 do require VIEW. A profile with no read key can still open most monitoring pages. — Fixed (MO-06, commit a66b23f).
  • Collection: editing needs config_write (metrics_admin.py:74-77) but the menu entry is only drawn inside the Administrator group, which requires user_manage (base.html:444, 989); operators can edit only via the URL. The Save/Run buttons render for everyone (collection.html:9-12, 63-75). — Fixed (MO-07/MO-08, commit c4f5ec3).
  • Scout settings: save requires config_write (app/views/settings.py:3352-3355) but the Scout settings group is admin-only in the settings nav (templates/settings/_nav.html:125); the disabled page offers "Open Scout settings" only to user_manage (scout/disabled.html:10). — Fixed (MO-09, decision: save requires user_manage, matching the admin-only pane; owned by AD-19, commit 4742a0a).
  • Analysis shows "Save pattern" and "Run deep capture" to every user (templates/analysis/index.html:100, 236) although the routes need user_manage / config_write (analysis.py:221-223, 300-302). — Fixed (MO-10, commit c4f5ec3).
  • Analysis deep JSON endpoints (wpp-matrix, subelements, orphans, deep/inventory, deep/objects, deep/wpp/…, deep/policy/…) do not apply visible_appliances(); with no device filter they span all appliances, and the drill-downs accept any appliance id (app/views/analysis.py:253-330; app/services/analysis_deep.py:96-104, 122-134). — Fixed (MO-11/12/13, commit fb6fc14).
  • Architecture "Fetch MAC addresses" opens an SSH session with only login_required (app/views/architecture.py:148-150). — Partly fixed (MO-06: the route now needs a read permission (view); no config_write gate or audit row was added, commit a66b23f). — Fixed (MO-14, decision: config_write gate, audit entry architecture.fetch_macs, button hidden without it, commit 2705393).
  • Analytics "Create board" is a native form post (templates/monitoring/analytics.html:308) to an endpoint that returns JSON (monitor_analytics.py:182-200); analytics.js only intercepts the panel form (static/js/analytics.js:984-986), so the browser displays raw JSON. — Fixed (MO-15, commit 8f8d97e).
  • Routes with no UI: board update (monitor_analytics.py:212), probe unmute (monitor_probes.py:633), store snapshot/snapshots/stores (metrics_admin.py:147, 223, 246); peer health is passed to collection.html (metrics_admin.py:56) but never rendered. — Fixed (MO-16 commit 8f8d97e; MO-17 commit 7d34b8c; MO-18/MO-19 commit c4f5ec3).
  • Service Monitor discovery modal says REST telemetry is "FortiWeb only" (_probe_page.html:481-488) but discovery creates licence/token probes on FortiAuthenticator (deep_monitor.py:2047-2048, 2110-2175). The CPU/memory form note says "works on FortiWeb and FortiADC" (_probe_page.html ~345) although FortiAuthenticator (REST) and FortiAnalyzer are supported. — Fixed (MO-20/MO-21, commit 7d34b8c).
  • inventory_snapshot (needed for the Metrics trend; metrics/index.html:447) is not in the seed plan (deploy/satom_cli/cmd_fix.py:38-70). — Fixed (MO-22, decision: seed a daily inventory_snapshot at 23:50 for new seeds, commit cb2a63f).
  • Report fleet section is stored but not rendered in report_detail.html, render_text or to_csv (monitor_reports.py:282 vs templates/monitoring/report_detail.html). — Fixed (MO-23, decision: render it in report_detail.html, render_text and to_csv, commit cb2a63f).
  • Logs view passes TROUBLESHOOT presets to the template (app/views/logs.py:44) which never uses them; log history is not filtered by ADOM (app/services/logcollect.py:198-216). — Partly fixed (MO-25: log history and file view now list/serve only logs of visible devices; the unused presets remain, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (MO-24: unused presets argument dropped, commit c4f5ec3).
  • Internal identifiers in shipped UI text: DNS Lookup entry placeholder/label example uses an internal domain and private IP (templates/dns_lookup/index.html:34, 37); the HTTPS probe URL placeholder uses a private IP and the Name placeholder a lab device name (_probe_page.html:301, 314); the infra-health loading text names an internal backup host label (templates/_infra_health.html:41). — Fixed (MO-26/MO-28 commit c4f5ec3; MO-27 commit 7d34b8c).
  • dns_tool.py:6 says DNS servers are managed in "Settings → admin console"; the UI is Settings → Network & DNS → DNS Lookup (templates/settings/_nav.html:100-101). — Fixed (MO-29, commit c4f5ec3).
  • Metric labels: FortiADC collector publishes RTT series without a policy label (device level) under the same names FortiWeb uses per policy (metrics_collect.py:516-530 vs 361-369), so selectors such as satom_policy_client_rtt_ms{policy=~"$policy"} never match FortiADC. — Fixed (MO-30, commit cb2a63f).

Stale or wrong in the old documentation#

  • user-guide.md:258-259 and :1514-1515 — "⏰ Schedule button on Server Policy for operators". No such control exists in app/templates/workspace/ or any JS; scheduling user-scope actions is done from Automation → Automations (app/templates/partials/nav_automation.html:64-66).
  • user-guide.md:1514 — Scheduled Actions under "FortiWeb ADOM → Administrator". The entries are now Automation → Automations / System Automations in every ADOM (app/templates/partials/nav_automation.html:30-71).
  • user-guide.md:1523 — deep_monitor "every 5 minutes" (also app/services/scheduled_actions.py:310) while the seed plan creates it every 3 minutes (deploy/satom_cli/cmd_fix.py:45-46). — Fixed (AU-29, commit d4bb9cb).
  • user-guide.md:1527 — "the full upgrade — destructive, fixed date/time, and only inside an approved Change Request window" implies it flashes. _do_upgrade is a stub that never flashes and returns ok=False — app/services/scheduled_actions.py:1450-1463. — Partly fixed (AU-17: catalog text, change page badge and docs now say a scheduled upgrade closes failed and firmware is flashed live; executor still does not flash and upgrade stays schedulable, commit 2a2019f).
  • user-guide.md:1550-1551 — CR workflow "draft → notify → approve → schedule". Notify is not a state; the states are draft/approved/scheduled/in_progress/completed/failed/cancelled (app/models.py:1534-1535); "Mark notified" is an independent action.
  • user-guide.md:4555-4556 — External approval "Withdrawing an approval makes it un-runnable again" / §35.4 implies an integration can approve. record_external_approval (app/services/cr_orchestrator.py:223) has no caller in app/ or deploy/ (only tests); no route, hook result or API writes external_approved_at. An External-mode CR can never run. — Fixed (AU-07, decision: POST /api/v1/change-requests/<id>/external-approval (admin scope) plus console Record/Withdraw for user_manage, commit 87bb23e).
  • user-guide.md:4537-4538 — "Keys SATOM understands in a change.requested result: crq_ref and crq_url, which are written onto the change request". No code reads hook results back into a CR (hook_runner.py stores data in the status file only; record_crq callers are only change_requests.py:1353 and cr_orchestrator.py:182 for the native tracker). Same false claim in the starter source comment app/services/hook_starters.py:60-62 and the flash at app/views/change_requests.py:1275-1276. — Fixed (AU-01, decision: implement write-back, a successful change.requested run's crq_ref/crq_url is recorded on the CR; starter comment and flash aligned, commit f444c58).
  • user-guide.md:4502-4505 — starters "a working script you own the moment you save it". The starters only define def run(ctx) (app/services/hook_starters.py:38, 81, 119, 165) and never call it nor import ctx; the runner executes hook.py as a script (app/services/hook_runner.py:318), so a starter does nothing and is graded ok (hook_runner.py:367-375). They also use resp.status_code, but the SDK response only has status (app/services/integration_sdk.py:75-78) — AttributeError once fixed to run. — Fixed (AU-02, AU-03, commit f444c58).
  • user-guide.md:4491-4492 — events window.opening / window.closing listed as general events. They are dispatched only inside open_window / close_window after a NetBox call (app/services/cr_orchestrator.py:339, 377), so without NetBox configured they never fire. window.closing sends outcome "ok"/"failed" (cr_orchestrator.py:378) while the catalog promises "completed | failed | cancelled | in_progress" (app/services/integration_hooks.py:187). — Fixed (AU-04, AU-05, commit 2a2019f).
  • user-guide.md:4609-4613 — "a one-shot is already an absolute moment" for scheduled actions. The scheduled-action form stores once_at verbatim (app/views/scheduled_actions.py:187-188) and compares it to UTC (app/services/scheduler.py:91-98); no timezone conversion, unlike CR windows (app/views/change_requests.py:141-155). — Fixed (AU-06, commit d4bb9cb).
  • user-guide.md:4659-4660 — export "with the first five ticked by default". Default columns are device, policy, vserver, service, status (app/services/prep_store.py:61-62), not the first five of the list (device, kind, host, policy, vserver).
  • user-guide.md:4575-4581 — Action list omits HA failover and administrator-defined documentary types (app/views/change_requests.py:40-41, 88-96).
  • user-guide.md:4671-4672 — document "English or German" only; other languages are offered once translated and enabled (app/services/cr_document.py:84-130).
  • user-guide.md:5758 — Integration hook step "from Administrator → Integrations"; the page is Settings → Integrations (app/templates/settings/_nav.html:85-86; url_prefix /settings/integrations).
  • user-guide.md:5657 — Process "Administrator → Process, in every ADOM" is true, but that Administrator group is shown only to user_manage (app/templates/base.html:369-383), so operators with config_write cannot reach it from the menu. — Fixed (AU-18, commit d4bb9cb).

Inconsistencies between code, UI and configuration#

  • External approval mode is fail-closed but has no writer: record_external_approval unused (app/services/cr_orchestrator.py:223); UI offers "External — an integration must approve it" (app/templates/change_requests/_new_form.html, approval select). Such a change stays "waiting for external change approval" forever. — Fixed (AU-07, decision: API v1 external-approval endpoint (admin scope) plus console Record/Withdraw, commit 87bb23e).
  • A live firmware push closes the whole CR from that one appliance's outcome (app/views/appliances.py:1170, 1337), so in a multi-appliance CR only the first appliance can ever be flashed live; _change_authorization then finds no open candidate (app/views/appliances.py:973-979). — Fixed (AU-08, commit 2a2019f).
  • CR "Schedule" after the window start has passed creates a one-shot with next_run = None (app/services/change_requests.py:500 + app/services/scheduler.py:98), which due_actions never selects (app/services/scheduled_actions.py:2253-2265); the CR sits in "scheduled" until it is run by hand. — Fixed (AU-09, commit 2a2019f).
  • approve() performs no status check (app/services/change_requests.py:112-140); only the template hides the button for non-draft states (app/templates/change_requests/_view.html:35). A direct POST can re-approve a cancelled/completed CR. Same for cancel() (change_requests.py:143-155) on terminal CRs. — Fixed (AU-10, AU-11, commit 2a2019f).
  • "Mark notified" posts no recipients field (app/templates/change_requests/_view.html:60-64; app/views/change_requests.py:1204), so the notice goes to Settings → Email default recipients, never to the CR's "Notify on completion" list; the card text says "sending is out of scope" (_view.html:447) although the button sends e-mail when SMTP is configured. — Fixed (AU-12, AU-13, commit 2a2019f).
  • Documentary change types: the refusal says "close this change request by hand" (app/services/change_requests.py:246-250) but there is no route to mark a CR completed; only Cancel exists. — Fixed (AU-14, commit 2a2019f).
  • Scheduled-action "Next run" column renders naive UTC with no label (app/templates/scheduled_actions/index.html:157) while the page timezone for daily/weekly/monthly is the console timezone. — Fixed (AU-15, commit d4bb9cb).
  • last_status = 'missed' (app/scheduler_runtime.py:75) is not rendered by the list template (only ok/failed/skipped/running, index.html:160-169) and shows "—". — Fixed (AU-16, commit d4bb9cb).
  • Upgrade spec summary and _do_upgrade docstring claim authorization/execution; executor is a stub (app/services/scheduled_actions.py:1450-1463), yet upgrade is offered as a schedulable CR type. — Partly fixed (AU-17: spec summary, docstring, CR badge and docs now say a scheduled upgrade closes failed; executor still does not flash and upgrade stays schedulable from the Upgrade Flow, commit 2a2019f).
  • Process: nav entry gated on view (app/templates/partials/nav_process.html:18) but included only inside the user_manage Administrator group (app/templates/base.html:369, 383). run_detail (app/views/process.py:334-347) and the index "Recent runs" (process.py:142-143) are not ADOM-scoped, unlike _proc_or_404. — Partly fixed (AU-19/20: run detail, resume and Recent runs now follow the process's ADOM; nav placement unchanged, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (AU-18: Process shown to non-user_manage users in its own Automation group, commit d4bb9cb).
  • Calendar "What already ran" band reads all ScheduledActionRun rows without ADOM scoping (app/views/calendar.py:299-331) while the automation band is scoped (calendar.py:263-265). — Fixed (AU-21, commit fb6fc14).
  • Lease locks are client-side only: object-editor save endpoints never check the lease (app/views/objedit.py:478-520); /api/locks/steal has no permission or ADOM check (app/views/locks.py:70-78); the inline editor (partial=1, objedit/_body.html) loads no lock guard (app/templates/objedit/editor.html:14-18). — Partly fixed (AU-24: acquire/steal/status now limited to visible devices, so no ADOM bypass; no permission check added, save endpoints and inline editor unchanged, commit fb6fc14). — Fixed (AU-22, AU-23 decision: acquire/heartbeat/steal require config_write, AU-25, commit f7f19a2).
  • Integrations "Scheduled reconciliation" field label "Virtual machines per round" (app/templates/integrations/index.html:309) but the parameter is appliances per round (per_round, app/services/netbox_client.py:425-435). — Fixed (AU-26, commit d4bb9cb).
  • Hook secret values: the editor declares names only; no form or route calls integration_hooks.set_secret (app/services/integration_hooks.py:580); values can only come from SATOM_HOOK_SECRET_<NAME> or direct vault writes. — Fixed (AU-27, decision: write-only Secret values card in the hook editor (user_manage, audited), commit f444c58).
  • device_sync/device_inspect summaries say "FortiWeb/FortiADC/FortiAnalyzer" while products include FortiAuthenticator (app/services/scheduled_actions.py:256-272). — Fixed (AU-28, commit d4bb9cb).
  • deep_monitor catalog text "Schedule EVERY 5 MINUTES" vs seed plan 3 minutes (scheduled_actions.py:310 vs deploy/satom_cli/cmd_fix.py:45-46). — Fixed (AU-29, commit d4bb9cb).
  • The task brief associated operations.template_approve with change requests; in code it gates only template/provisioning approval (app/views/templates.py:293, 341, 358; app/views/provisioning.py:295, 312). CR approval is user_manage.

Not documented (and why)#

  • git_bundle handler internals and the retired scheduled bundle — retired, listed in the catalog table only.
  • /_updiag upload diagnostics beacon in jobs.js — internal debugging channel, not a user feature.
  • Machine-translation token/cost counters on the Change Types page — UI detail of the translator service owned by another area.
  • services/deep_jobs.py — predecessor job store used by deep monitors; covered by the monitoring area.
  • Exact text of each per-language change-document section — owned by cr_document.py prose and too large to reproduce; summarised in change-control.
  • No new extra articles were created; change-control is filed as a child of change-requests.
